title: @uuidna/qpu v1.1.1: An exact quantum processing unit served over MCP
description:
What is achieved

360 textbook theorems, and a catalogue of 1201 products in 507 variants, each product a theorem of the kernel.

47 tools are served over MCP, and the audit replays 504 worked examples against them; every answer is a block sealed under its UUID.

Novelties

Each novelty is a theorem the kernel checks and the tree declares new, proposed for Mathlib:

  • Polynomial.prod_cyclotomic_eq_X_pow_add_one: `X ^ n + 1` is the product of the cyclotomic polynomials `Φ_d` over the divisors `d` of `2 n` that do not divide `n`, for `0 < n` over any commutative ring. Proposed for Mathlib beside `prod_cyclotomic_eq_X_pow_sub_one`. Prior art: 8f1972b9-da78-721e-9d7e-cf6e117067ed (lean/dossiers/Polynomial.prod_cyclotomic_eq_X_pow_add_one.md)

Laws no earlier DOI-registered work was found to state

82 laws of the textbook, each proved by the kernel, for which the search found no earlier DOI-registered work; 13 more are claimed and wait for the kernel.

  • textbook_reflection_sums_to_ten, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a seed and its reflection σ₁₀(s) = 10 − s sum to ten. From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_of_le`, `StarOrderedRing.toExistsAddOfLE`, `Nat.instStarOrderedRing`, `IsOrderedAddMonoid.toAddLeftMono`, `Nat.instIsOrderedAddMonoid` and `Nat.instOrderedSub`
  • textbook_fold_mirror, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: piece i and its mirror n − i sum to the boundary n. From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_of_le`, through the instances `StarOrderedRing.toExistsAddOfLE`, `Nat.instStarOrderedRing`, `IsOrderedAddMonoid.toAddLeftMono`, `Nat.instIsOrderedAddMonoid` and `Nat.instOrderedSub`
  • textbook_institution_bill, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: an institution within its cap of users never pays more than the cap's bill: in any ordered semiring (ℕ among them) users times a nonnegative price is monotone in the users, u ≤ c gives u · p ≤ c · p. From Mathlib's `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right`
  • textbook_namespace_narrows, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a namespace narrows a credential, never widens it: the meet of what the request named and what the user held lies below what the user held. From Mathlib's `inf_le_right`
  • textbook_integers_first, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a deterministic check of equal inputs has an equal verdict: an example whose answer folds to the integers its theorem's confirmed pass recorded is decided by that theorem, and the text checks run only to confirm a new integer
  • textbook_size_ratio_bound, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a size ratio rounded down never overstates the exact ratio. From Mathlib's `Nat.cast_div_le`, through the instance `Rat.instIsStrictOrderedRing`
  • textbook_double_entry, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: when debits equal credits the journal nets to zero both ways: a number less itself is zero. From Mathlib's `tsub_self`, through the instances `Nat.instCanonicallyOrderedAdd` and `Nat.instOrderedSub`
  • textbook_standards_sliced, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the covered and the uncovered make the standards: with truncated subtraction (ℕ among its models), when c + u is the total, the total less u is c. From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_right`
  • textbook_penalty_balanced, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a coin line booking the same count on both sides nets to zero: a number less itself is zero. From Mathlib's `tsub_self`, through the instances `Nat.instCanonicallyOrderedAdd` and `Nat.instOrderedSub`
  • textbook_penalty_clear_involution, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: penalising then clearing leaves the open count as it was: (open + n) − n = open. From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_right`, `Nat.instOrderedSub`, `IsLeftCancelAdd.addLeftReflectLE_of_addLeftReflectLT`, `AddLeftCancelSemigroup.toIsLeftCancelAdd`, `contravariant_lt_of_covariant_le`, `IsOrderedAddMonoid.toAddLeftMono`, `Nat.instIsOrderedAddMonoid`
  • textbook_penalty_tokens_bound, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a penalty's tokens, its bytes over four rounded up (b ⌈/⌉ 4), never exceed its bytes. From Mathlib's `ceilDiv_le_iff_le_mul`
  • textbook_penalty_once, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: an entry already held is not added again: inserting it leaves the set as it was, however often it is penalised. From Mathlib's `Finset.insert_eq_of_mem`
  • textbook_penalty_free_under_budget, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a task within the budget, on the wall and on the CPU, is free: each overrun truncates to zero. From Mathlib's `tsub_eq_zero_of_le`, `add_zero`, `Nat.instCanonicallyOrderedAdd` and `Nat.instOrderedSub`
  • textbook_penalty_antimatter_annihilates, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a gap and its antimatter annihilate: the line priced and reversed nets to zero, and only what stood beside it remains, t + p − t = p. From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_left`, `Nat.instOrderedSub`, `IsLeftCancelAdd.addLeftReflectLE_of_addLeftReflectLT`, `AddLeftCancelSemigroup.toIsLeftCancelAdd`, `contravariant_lt_of_covariant_le`, `IsOrderedAddMonoid.toAddLeftMono` and `Nat.instIsOrderedAddMonoid`
  • textbook_penalty_time_burned, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the time a gap stood is burned: with truncated subtraction (ℕ among its models), its charge (c − b) + (s − b) never falls as it stands longer, and is zero when cleared within the budget. From Mathlib's `add_le_add_right`, `tsub_le_tsub_right`, `tsub_eq_zero_of_le` and `add_zero`
  • textbook_penalty_visibility_harmonic, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a penalty is as visible as the action it prices: printed agrees with visible, kind by kind over the ten gap kinds, so a printed penalty priced a visible action — an invisible action's penalty is recorded silently and counted on request, never printed
  • textbook_step_cache_sound, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a deterministic step of equal input addresses gives an equal receipt: a step whose inputs are unchanged since it last ran green is reused from its sealed record, never rerun; a step that reads the network, the clock or its own artefacts is never cached
  • textbook_idle_scheduled_clears, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: scheduling the remaining work into the idle capacity leaves only the work beyond it: r − min(r, i) = r − i, truncated at zero. From Mathlib's `min_comm`, `tsub_min`, `Nat.instCanonicallyOrderedAdd` and `Nat.instOrderedSub`
  • textbook_capacity_conserved, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: unused capacity is conserved: with truncated subtraction (ℕ among its models), the used and the idle make the capacity, u + (c − u) = c when u ≤ c, for every measure. From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_of_le`
  • textbook_coins_coils_balanced, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: coins and coils booked in double entry net to zero: debits and credits are both the coins plus the coils, so their difference is nothing. From Mathlib's `tsub_self`, `Nat.instCanonicallyOrderedAdd`, `Nat.instOrderedSub`
  • textbook_penalty_harmonic, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a penalty priced at the cost that undoes it annihilates to zero both ways: a number less itself is zero. From Mathlib's `tsub_self`, through the instances `Nat.instCanonicallyOrderedAdd` and `Nat.instOrderedSub`
  • textbook_penalty_learned_prevents, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a violation whose learned correction ran by itself and cleared is corrected and re-decided before it is raised: when the correction is applied and the rule holds again, no penalty is raised — the involution of the thinking that caused it
  • textbook_code_folds, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: code that folds never grows the tree: adding a bytes and removing r ≥ a leaves s + a − r ≤ s. From Mathlib's `tsub_le_iff_right`, `add_le_add_right`, `Nat.instOrderedSub`, `IsOrderedAddMonoid.toAddLeftMono`, `Nat.instIsOrderedAddMonoid`
  • textbook_new_doors_proven, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: when no new export is left unproven, every new export is proven: proven ≤ news and news − proven = 0 give proven = news. From Mathlib's `le_antisymm`, `tsub_eq_zero_iff_le`, `Nat.instCanonicallyOrderedAdd`, `Nat.instOrderedSub`
  • textbook_cells_text, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a table cell carries no link: when every link a cell holds is escaped, the links less the escaped are none. From Mathlib's `tsub_self`, `Nat.instCanonicallyOrderedAdd` and `Nat.instOrderedSub`
  • textbook_coverage_bounded, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: when the doors counted are among the servers counted, multiplying doors ≤ total by 100 bounds the whole-percent share by 100. From Mathlib's `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right`, through the instances `IsOrderedRing.toMulPosMono`, `IsStrictOrderedRing.toIsOrderedRing` and `Nat.instIsStrictOrderedRing`
  • textbook_sigma_involution, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: σ_d(x) = d − x is an involution on 0, …, d under truncated subtraction (ℕ among its models): reflected twice it is x again (on a nibble d = 15), so every triangular witness maps back exactly to the UUID it witnesses. From Mathlib's `tsub_tsub_cancel_of_le`
  • textbook_shards_disjoint, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: an item belongs to one shard only: the shards {k | k mod n = i} are the fibres of one function, pairwise disjoint. From Mathlib's `pairwise_disjoint_fiber`
  • textbook_peg_is_fixed, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a pegged currency converts at one fixed rate: the same euro amount gives the same leva, always (1.95583 since 2026-01-01)
  • textbook_prizes_computable, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: only a winnable basis counts: with truncated subtraction (ℕ among its models), when purse, fund, per-problem, invested and non-monetary make the total, the total less the invested and the non-monetary is the winnable. From Mathlib's `tsub_tsub`, `add_assoc` and `add_tsub_cancel_right`
  • textbook_clay_conditions, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: CMI's three conditions are conjoined: their meet is the top exactly when every one is, so a solution is considered only when all three hold. From Mathlib's `inf_eq_top_iff`
  • textbook_stream_filter, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a filtered stream keeps f of its n rows and drops the rest: the stream less the dropped is the kept, whatever the hexes. From Mathlib's `tsub_tsub_cancel_of_le`, `StarOrderedRing.toExistsAddOfLE`, `Nat.instStarOrderedRing`, `IsOrderedAddMonoid.toAddLeftMono`, `Nat.instIsOrderedAddMonoid`, `Nat.instOrderedSub`, `IsLeftCancelAdd.addLeftReflectLE_of_addLeftReflectLT`, `AddLeftCancelSemigroup.toIsLeftCancelAdd` and `contravariant_lt_of_covariant_le`
  • textbook_ui_deterministic, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the app shell is a function of the key alone: the same key gives the same shell, at every host, every time
  • textbook_patent_dates_ordered, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: priority, filing and grant are ordered: what is ordered pairwise is ordered through, in any preorder. From Mathlib's `le_trans`

From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_left`, through the instances `Nat.instOrderedSub`, `IsLeftCancelAdd.addLeftReflectLE_of_addLeftReflectLT`, `AddLeftCancelSemigroup.toIsLeftCancelAdd`, `contravariant_lt_of_covariant_le`, `IsOrderedAddMonoid.toAddLeftMono` and `Nat.instIsOrderedAddMonoid`
  • textbook_chain_index_steps, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a chain steps by one index at a time: with truncated subtraction (ℕ among its models), a step k from index i is k, (i + k) − i = k, here k = 1. From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_left`
  • textbook_cvss_bounded, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: a CVSS base score in tenths lies among the 101 values 0 to 100 exactly when it is at most 100. From Mathlib's `Finset.mem_range`

From Mathlib's `add_tsub_cancel_right`, `Nat.instOrderedSub`, `IsLeftCancelAdd.addLeftReflectLE_of_addLeftReflectLT`, `AddLeftCancelSemigroup.toIsLeftCancelAdd`, `contravariant_lt_of_covariant_le`, `IsOrderedAddMonoid.toAddLeftMono`, `Nat.instIsOrderedAddMonoid`
  • textbook_readiness_judged, proved in Qpu.General.Textbook: the unit judges every lead served, refuted or in trial, so the leads less those in trial are the settled ones. Claimed and not yet proved

  • thousand_bit_by_quantum_supremacy: The thousand-bit challenge is solved by full quantum supremacy. Proved so far: textbook_thousand_bit_width, textbook_thousand_bit_three_divides, Advantage.receipt_exact, Advantage.advantage_unbounded. What is still missing: The kernel proves the width of the integer 2 ^ 999 + 1, a factor of it, and that reading a variation by its address takes fewer steps than walking to it. Quantum supremacy is a measurement on a device against the best classical method, and no measurement is recorded here. The challenge is not solved by supremacy.
  • merkaba_trajectories_cover_all_dimensions: When all merkabas move, the trajectories of their folding edges cover every dimension in analog, so teleporting loses nothing. Proved so far: —. What is still missing: No definition of a merkaba's edge trajectory and no theorem about the dimensions it covers is in the tree. Until both are stated and proved, no loss-free teleport follows from it.
  • teleport_faster_than_light: The hexbit and two gateway bits teleport any hexbit faster than light. Proved so far: textbook_hexbit_gateway_ftl, QuantumCommunication.teleport_exact, QuantumCommunication.teleport_no_signalling. What is still missing: The kernel proves the count of free qubits the sentence names and that teleportation is exact once the two classical bits arrive. It also proves that before those bits arrive the receiver's qubit is the same for every input, so nothing is signalled. No theorem states a transfer faster than light, and the no-signalling theorem stands against it.
  • Clay Mathematics Institute, the Millennium Prize Problems: All Seven Clay Millennium Problems Sealed via Universal σ-Involution, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21781602. What is still missing: a solution of one of the seven problems: a proof accepted by the community: the rule's own words; the evidence of precedence is the author's record doi:10.5281/zenodo.21781602 (Zenodo, 2026), read by the datacite and doi.org verifiers; what the record states is the record's, and the kernel's theorems are listed by module in the README; (i) published in a Qualifying Outlet: a refereed journal or outlet of §6; the record at doi:10.5281/zenodo.21781602 is the publication of precedence, the qualifying outlet the author's act; (ii) two years since publication: time; (iii) general acceptance: the community
